acceptance: VERIFY: A fast-tier unit test fails on a branch that adds an unregistered module- or session-scoped autouse fixture, naming the fixture and the allowlist file; it passes on develop after the existing such fixtures are registered
VERIFY: The allowlist lists every current non-function-scoped autouse fixture with owner, rationale and expiry; expired entries fail the test with a message asking for re-justification
VERIFY: Mutation check recorded: removing an entry, or adding a synthetic module-scoped autouse fixture in a test conftest, makes the test fail
GUARDRAIL: Registration is data in the allowlist file, never source comments (comment policy); the test adds under 2 s to the fast tier (measured)
GUARDRAIL: No existing fixture behavior changes in this PR
context: Source: CI time-regression incident of 2026-10-25 and an independent adversarial review of the prevention plan. PR #3423 added an autouse module-scoped fixture (tests/conftest.py, _chdb_connections_closed_after_module) that opened a chDB probe session after every module; the fast-tier pytest time went from 327.81 s (run 40143597290) to 1041.10 s (run 40195371347) and PR CI wall time from about 12 to 20+ minutes for about 18 hours before anyone noticed. No CI check measured test time: _project/scripts/fast_lane_ceiling_check.py checks marker composition only, and tests/duration_policy.py's per-test T1 budget is refreshed from nightly data and never sees module-teardown cost spread across tests. Pre-incident fast-job wall time varied 7.8-18.0 min (cv about 19%), so job wall time cannot be a blocking signal; summed per-test junit time is the blocking metric.
description: Catch the #3423 class at review time, before any timing exists: a fast-tier unit test introspects every tests/**/conftest.py (and pytest plugins registered there) for autouse fixtures whose scope is not 'function' and asserts the set equals a committed allowlist. Each allowlist entry records the fixture's qualified name, owner, rationale and an expiry date (mirroring the quarantine marker's metadata discipline). Adding such a fixture then becomes a visible, reviewed decision in the PR diff. Prior art: quarantine marker metadata; quality/comment-policy.json registry pattern. New pattern for fixtures.
